title: OSV-backed SBOM Security scanning
description: Security observes canonical SBOM references and explicit scan intents, normalizes SBOM/package/PURL/commit targets, queries OSV, persists scan facts, publishes canonical Nostr observables, evaluates policy-scoped thresholds, and dispatches notifications only for new or materially changed policy breaches.
in_scope: Event-driven SBOM-triggered OSV scans from accepted canonical SBOM reference and availability observables.
Explicit ContextVM scan/rescan intents for SBOM references, package coordinates, PURLs, and Git commits.
Security scan status, scan summary, target summary, finding detail, and audit event contracts using canonical kinds 30315, 30900, 30078, and 4903.
Policy-scoped Security settings, latest-scan freshness gates, scheduled rescans, breach fingerprinting, and notification dispatch semantics.
Deterministic test and verification expectations for subsequent implementation epics.
Compatibility aggregate projection updates from latest successful Security scans without mutating canonical SBOM events.
out_of_scope: Implementing scanner orchestration, repositories, migrations, OSV adapter expansion, policy integration, notification integration, or application wiring in Epic 1.
Allocating a new Bahia-specific Nostr kind for Security events.
Mutating canonical SBOM events after a Security scan completes.
Synchronous deployment blocking that waits for a new OSV scan by timeout or polling.
preconditions: SBOM generation/import publishes canonical 30078 SBOM reference events and 30004 availability lists with accepted relay OKs.
ContextVM kind 25910 is the canonical mutation intent transport, normally wrapped with 1059 or 21059 for sensitive payloads.
Bahia clients and services can subscribe to canonical observables with scoped filters and process EOSE/CLOSED/AUTH outcomes.
postconditions: Every Security scan run has durable persisted state and corresponding Nostr status/audit/summary evidence or a tracked publish retry state.
Clients treat ContextVM responses as acknowledgments only and derive durable scan truth from Security observables.
Policy breaches are deduplicated by stable fingerprint and notification delivery is limited to new or materially changed breaches.
happy_paths: An accepted SBOM reference event triggers a non-blocking Security scan; the scanner verifies the payload hash, queries OSV, publishes running/completed status, summaries, findings, and audit facts with relay OK verification.

An operator publishes security/scan for a package, PURL, commit, or SBOM reference; Bahia acknowledges accepted intent and the requester follows correlated Security observables until terminal scan state appears.

A latest completed Security scan breaches an environment-scoped policy threshold; Bahia records a breach fingerprint, publishes a security policy-breach audit fact, and dispatches security.policy_breached once.
failure_paths: Relay OK rejection, CLOSED, or AUTH requirements prevent publication; the implementation records explicit publish failure/retry state rather than marking observables published.
OSV invalid-request responses are classified as non-retryable scan errors with operator-visible status/audit evidence.
Missing, malformed, or hash-mismatched SBOM payloads fail the scan without changing canonical SBOM events.
Policy requires a fresh completed scan but none exists; gate behavior follows explicit policy settings rather than launching a synchronous wait.
edge_cases: Large SBOMs require deduplication and OSV batch chunking without losing query-result order.
CPE-only packages are persisted with an unsupported_coordinate reason rather than silently ignored.
PURLs that already include a version must not also send top-level version to OSV.
Recurring scans with unchanged breach fingerprints must not duplicate notifications.
Withdrawn OSV advisories remain historically visible as withdrawn findings instead of being deleted.
non_functional_requirements: No polling, repeated peek subscriptions, sleeps, or timeout-based completion detection for Nostr event delivery.
Inbound Nostr events must be validated before trust and handlers must be idempotent by event id and target key.
Every Security publish must verify relay OK accepted flag and rejection message; batch publishes must handle partial failure.
Sensitive payloads, raw OSV hydrated records, credentials, private repository URLs where policy marks them sensitive, and notification secrets must not be exposed in public Nostr content.
Tests must be deterministic and inject EVENT, EOSE, OK, CLOSED, and AUTH outcomes directly.
dependencies: Existing deployment policy scope and vulnerability threshold rules

ambiguities.description: Raw hydrated OSV vulnerability cache retention is recommended as 30 days in the plan, but product/legal retention requirements are not yet approved.
Expected steady-state scan volume is unknown; partitioning and cache sizing may require operator input before high-volume deployment.

human_decisions: Use existing canonical kinds 25910, 30315, 30900, 30078, 4903, and existing SBOM 30004 availability lists for the Security contract; no new Bahia-specific kind is allocated in Epic 1.
